correctness.rationale: Radial integration gives 2pi G_q(x)/x for G_q(x)=J_1(x)-qJ_1(qx), and area pi(1-q^2)>0 at zero. Put H(x)=xJ_1(x). Then H'=xJ_0 and H''=H'/x-H, so (H^2+H'^2)'=2H'^2/x, strictly increasing in the integrated sense on every positive interval. At a root H(x)=H(qx), this forces |J_0(x)|>q|J_0(qx)|. Consequently G_{q,x}=J_0(x)-q^2J_0(qx) is nonzero there and of the sign of J_0(x). At each J_0 gap endpoint, the same energy comparison gives |J_1(x)|>q|J_1(qx)|; alternating signs force one root per gap, and all simple crossings inside a gap have the same orientation, so there cannot be two. Below the first endpoint the integral has positive integrand almost everywhere. The implicit-function theorem gives analytic roots. The inner argument y=qx has derivative xJ_0(x)/G_{q,x}>0. Its left limit is zero and its right limit is j_{0,n}: the normalized integral G_q/(1-q) extends smoothly to q=1 with value xJ_0(x), and its local branch at j_{0,n} is j_{0,n}[1+(1-q)/2]+O((1-q)^2), entering the correct open gap and hence coinciding with its unique root. This is the decisive endpoint argument, without assuming the right endpoint is not a zero of the limiting function. At q=0 the local J_1 branch and qJ_1(qx)=xq^2/2+O(q^4) give exactly the even disk expansion. Since x_n'=y J_0(y)/G_{q,x}, y's increasing range crosses just j_{0,1},...,j_{0,n-1}. At each crossing y'=x and J_0'(y)=-J_1(y); this gives the stated nonzero curvature and sign (-1)^(n+m). In particular the n=1 derivative is strictly negative, and H is strictly monotone on the gap so the equation for X_{n,m} determines it uniquely. Replay: RESULT.md lines 58–145 and the above argument; python3 /workspace/review_evidence/bounded_checks.py uses Bessel series and bisection to reproduce q_{2,1}=0.315585469056578 and X_{2,1}=7.620203695958628. The provided SciPy script and recorded outputs were inspected, not rerun; the infinite-order result rests on the strict energy and implicit branch argument.

value.rationale: The scalar annular Fourier transform is a natural object. A full radial zero enumeration and exactly n-1 alternating nondegenerate turns resolve the meaningful question of whether dark-ring radii move monotonically as the hole grows: the first does, all higher ones have a prescribed number of reversals. The exact locations and endpoint corrections are useful beyond the known endpoint optical profiles; no Laplacian or complex-zero significance is inferred.
